construct: IgG autoantibodies target desmoglein adhesion molecules within desmosomes, disrupting keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion. The resulting acantholysis produces fragile intraepidermal blisters, mucosal erosions, and a positive Nikolsky sign.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Painful oral erosions, flaccid bullae, Nikolsky positivity, and suprabasal acantholysis identify pemphigus vulgaris from desmoglein-directed autoimmunity.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Hemidesmosomal autoimmunity is the closest alternative because it also causes autoimmune blistering, but bullous pemphigoid produces a subepidermal split with tense blisters rather than suprabasal acantholysis and fragile mucosal disease.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Acantholysis is loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion, directly implicating desmoglein-containing desmosomes rather than basement-membrane anchoring structures.
